latin_text: It is a commonplace expression in the schools that man is a lesser world, in which are seen a body compounded from the elements, and a heavenly spirit, and the vegetative soul of plants, and the sense of brutes, and reason, and the angelic mind, and the likeness of God.
english_translation: It is a commonplace expression in the schools that man is a lesser world, in which are seen a body compounded from the elements, and a heavenly spirit, and the vegetative soul of plants, and the sense of brutes, and reason, and the angelic mind, and the likeness of God.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico invokes scholastic commonplace: humanity is a *lesser world* (*mundus minor*) containing all cosmic orders—elements, plants, animals, rational intellect, angelic mind, divine likeness. [INFERRED] The angelic mind is *within* the human soul as its highest faculty. This microcosmicstructure explains human dignity: humans recapitulate the entire cosmic hierarchy internally and can actualize every level.

The philosophical function is anthropological: understanding humans requires understanding their angelic component. The human soul is not merely rational but angelic at its apex. [INFERRED] This grounds mystical ascent: actualizing the angelic mind within oneself means ascending the inner ladder of one's own soul.

[VERIFIED] Commento (C.2.6) develops human as the bond between worlds. Oration (O.1.3) describes ascent through all levels. Being & Unity grounds it: the microcosmic soul participates in all degrees of being.
notes: HARVESTER passage: H.SP.5 | Human soul contains angelic intellect; man as microcosm mirrors angelic order
